graders.evidence:
## Review of PR #107: Confirm quotes through the PMS's async mode

**Verdict: request changes.** This is a backend PR. Moving to the PMS's async mode is the right fix for the timeouts. But the PMS docs say the webhook usually arrives within 50 ms, and the code isn't ready for that. On a normal day some confirmed quotes will stay `pending` forever. No error is logged and the PMS doesn't retry.

**What I read:** the description, the diff, CI (lint and unit-tests both pass), and a checkout of the PR including `docs/pms.md` and every caller. No review comments of any kind, from people or bots. The PR isn't stacked; its base is `main`.

**What I couldn't read:**
- **Ticket:** the title, branch, body and commit carry no `HOT-` key, so I had no ticket to open with `tracker`. I can't check the acceptance criteria.
- **Repo gaps:** the repo has no app or server file, no schema for `quotes`, and no tests. So I couldn't check how the new route is mounted, whether `quotes.status` accepts `'pending'`, or what CI's unit-tests actually run.

**Questions that came back empty:**
- Pattern fit: the new code matches the existing style.
- Comment abuse: there isn't any.
- The migration: it only adds a new table, so it is safe while old and new versions run side by side.

## Findings

**1. Quotes get stuck in `pending` when the webhook beats the database write. Must fix.**
Case: a quote with one room line. The PMS answers `202` with the block id and sends the webhook about 50 ms later. If that arrives before the `pms_blocks` row is saved, the webhook doesn't find the block. It answers `204`, and the PMS only retries after an error answer, so the event is gone. The quote stays `pending` forever.

The same race has two other outcomes:
- The last webhook marks the quote `confirmed`, then `confirmQuote` finishes and overwrites it with `pending`.
- With 3 room lines, block 1's webhook can arrive before block 2 is saved. The quote then shows as confirmed with 1 of 3 blocks.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  confirmQuote->>PMS: POST ?async=true
  PMS-->>confirmQuote: 202 {blockId}
  PMS->>webhook: block.created (≈50 ms)
  webhook->>DB: block unknown → 204, event lost
  confirmQuote->>DB: insert pms_blocks (too late)
```

Fix, roughly:
- Mark the quote `pending` before the loop, not after.
- Answer an error status (e.g. `409`) for an unknown block id, so the PMS retries. It retries up to 5 times over 10 minutes.
- Only confirm the quote when the number of confirmed blocks equals the number of room lines, not when "none are left unconfirmed".

Inline comment: `src/pms/webhooks.ts:16`, plus a short one on `src/quotes/confirm.ts:19` about where `pending` is set.

**2. A rejected block leaves the quote `pending` with no outcome. Needs your decision.**
Case: the PMS sends `status: "rejected"` for one of 3 blocks. The quote stays `pending` forever, and the other 2 blocks keep holding rooms in the PMS. Nobody finds out.

This is a business rule, not just code: should the quote fail, should the other blocks be released, and who gets told? I'd ask the author (and the product owner) rather than guess.

Inline comment: `src/pms/webhooks.ts:18`.

**3. A failure partway through, or a double click, holds rooms twice. Should fix.**
Case: 3 room lines, and the PMS returns a `500` on block 2. Block 1 is already held in the PMS and saved, but the quote's status hasn't changed and the user sees an error. When they click confirm again, block 1 is requested a second time. A double click does the same for every block.

The old code had the same weakness. Now it also leaves extra `pms_blocks` rows that the "all confirmed?" check counts. A cheap guard is to refuse to confirm a quote that is already `pending` or `confirmed`.

Inline comment: `src/quotes/confirm.ts:12`.

**4. Rolling back this deploy strands quotes. Check by hand.**
If you roll back while quotes are `pending`, the webhook route goes away and those quotes never reach `confirmed`. Also check these before merging:
- the webhook URL is registered with the PMS in every environment;
- `quotes.status` accepts `'pending'`. If it has a check constraint, the first confirm fails;
- anything that reads `status = 'confirmed'` copes with the new in-between state.

I couldn't see any of these from the repo. A PR-level comment fits better than an inline one.

**5. Anyone who can reach the webhook can confirm blocks. A question for the author.**
`/webhooks/pms` accepts any POST without checking who sent it. `docs/pms.md` doesn't mention signing. If the endpoint is reachable from outside, someone who knows a block id can mark it confirmed. Ask how the endpoint is protected (a signature, a network allowlist, or something else).

Inline comment: `src/pms/webhooks.ts:7`.

**6. Nothing tests this. Should fix together with #1.**
The repo has no test files, so CI's green unit-tests run says nothing about this change. The race in #1 is exactly what an integration test with a fake PMS that answers the webhook instantly would catch. That includes the webhook arriving before the row is saved, and a rejected block.

Inline comment: no line to attach it to, so it belongs in the review body.

**7. `reserveBlocks` is now unused. Minor.**
It is dead code once this merges; delete it. Inline comment: `src/pms/client.ts:3`.

## Recommendation

Request changes, driven by #1 and #2. #1 will happen routinely in production, and #2 needs an answer before the design is final. #3 and #6 are cheap to fix in the same pass. #4 and #5 are questions, and #7 is optional.

My verdict is **request changes**. The new async flow has a timing bug. The PMS's own docs say its callback usually arrives within 50 ms, which is faster than this code saves the block it is waiting for. Under load, group quotes will get stuck in `pending` and nothing brings them back.

**What I covered**
- **Read:** the description, the diff (4 files, nothing left out), CI (lint and unit tests both pass), and `docs/pms.md`. I also read the rest of the repo, which is small, to see who uses quote status and the PMS client.
- **Empty:** there are no review comments of any kind, from people or bots. The PR is not stacked; it targets `main` directly.
- **Not read: the ticket.** The branch name, title and description carry no `HOT-` key, and the `tracker` tool can only look up a ticket by its key. So I couldn't check the PR against its acceptance criteria.
- **Questions with findings:** business logic, deploy, design, tests.
- **Questions with nothing to raise:** simplicity, patterns, comments. The comments are short and useful.
- **Didn't check:** webhook authentication. The PMS docs say nothing about signatures, so I couldn't judge it.

## Findings

**1. The callback can beat the database write, and the block is then lost for good.** `src/pms/webhooks.ts:16`
Here is the sequence. The PMS answers `202` with the block id. It creates the block and calls our webhook about 50 ms later. Meanwhile `confirmQuote` is still about to save that id to `pms_blocks`. The webhook finds no row, decides "not a block we asked for", and answers `204`. The PMS treats any `2xx` as delivered and only retries after an error. So the event never comes again, and the quote stays `pending` forever.

```text
confirmQuote                       PMS                     webhook
  requestBlock ──────────────────► 202 {blockId}
                                   creates block ────────► POST block.created
                                                             lookup blockId → no row
                                                             204  (PMS won't retry)
  insert pms_blocks (blockId) ◄── too late
```

There is a second version of the same race. Even when every row gets saved in time, `confirmQuote` sets the quote to `pending` only after the loop (`src/quotes/confirm.ts:19`). If the last webhook lands first, it marks the quote `confirmed`, and then `confirmQuote` overwrites that with `pending`.

**My recommendation:** must fix. Set the quote to `pending` before asking the PMS for any block. For an unknown block id, answer with an error (e.g. `409` or `503`) so the PMS retries; it retries up to 5 times over 10 minutes. The cleaner fix is to send our own id with each request if the PMS supports that, but that needs checking against the PMS API.

**2. A rejected block leaves the quote `pending` forever, while the other blocks keep holding rooms.** `src/pms/webhooks.ts:24`
Take a quote with 3 room lines. 2 blocks come back `confirmed` and 1 comes back `rejected`. The count of blocks that aren't confirmed stays at 1, so the quote never moves. The two confirmed blocks keep holding rooms in the hotel's PMS, and nobody is told.

**My recommendation:** must fix, or the PR must say how it's handled. What a partial rejection should mean is a business decision: fail the quote, release the other blocks, or alert someone. **You should decide this with the author**, not me.

**3. If one block request fails halfway, retrying the confirmation books the earlier blocks twice.** `src/quotes/confirm.ts:13`
Block 1 is requested and saved, then the PMS fails on block 2. The quote's status never changes. The user retries, and block 1 is requested again, so the hotel now holds those rooms twice. The old code had the same weakness, so this isn't new. But the PR is the natural place to fix it, since it now records which blocks exist.

**My recommendation:** worth a comment, not a blocker. Skip room lines that already have a block in `pms_blocks` for this quote.

**4. Deploy and contract points to confirm by hand (no inline comment).**
- **`'pending'` is a new quote status.** No schema exists in this repo, so I couldn't see whether `quotes.status` has an enum or a check constraint. If it does, the update fails after the blocks were already requested. Please confirm the column accepts `'pending'`.
- **Nothing tells the web app when a quote becomes confirmed.** `GET /api/v1/quotes/:id` doesn't return `status`. Whatever shows "confirmed" today has to learn that `pending` exists and then poll for the change. Worth asking the author how the web app does this.
- **Rollout order isn't written down.** The migration must run first. The webhook route must be live in the app (this repo has no app entry point, so I couldn't check whether it's added). The PMS must be configured to call it. Only then should `confirmQuote` start using async mode. If the PMS is set up last, every confirmation done in the meantime gets stuck. A feature flag around the switch would make the rollout reversible.

**5. No tests in the PR.** CI is green, but no test file was changed and none exists in the repo. The race, the rejection path and the retry path are all untested. A single test that delivers the webhook before the insert finishes would have caught finding 1.

**My recommendation:** ask for tests of the webhook handler covering finding 1 and finding 2 alongside those fixes.

## Suggested action
**Request changes**, with inline comments on 1, 2 and 3, and 4 and 5 in the review body. I checked each line against the PR's head commit (`6636faa`):
- **Finding 1:** `src/pms/webhooks.ts:16`, the line that ignores unknown blocks. Mention `src/quotes/confirm.ts:19` in the same comment.
- **Finding 2:** `src/pms/webhooks.ts:24`, the check that only counts confirmed blocks.
- **Finding 3:** `src/quotes/confirm.ts:13`, the `requestBlock` call inside the loop.

Tell me which ones to post, or whether to change any of them. I won't post anything until you do.

The comment on line 15 assumes an unknown id is a stranger's block. Here it's usually our own block that we haven't stored yet.

Cheapest fix: answer non-2xx (for example `503`) for an unknown `blockId`, so the PMS retries. It retries up to 5 times over 10 minutes.

Three cases come from the same cause:

- **Confirmed after a failure:** same quote, but the PMS returns 500 for B. The user sees an error, yet A's webhook still marks the quote `confirmed` while holding only A's rooms.
- **Stuck in pending:** both webhooks arrive between the last insert and line 19. Line 19 then overwrites `confirmed` with `pending`, and nothing will ever set it back.

```text
confirmQuote
  for each block: requestBlock → insert row      ← webhooks can fire in here
  update quote → 'pending'                       ← runs last, can overwrite 'confirmed'
```

Fix direction:
- Set `pending` before the loop.
- Have the webhook only confirm once the quote knows it has finished requesting. For example, store the expected block count, or set a "requests done" flag after the loop.

This is a product decision: should the quote fail, release A, and notify someone? I'd raise it as a question, not prescribe the answer.
→ **Recommend: inline comment, asked as a question.**

**4. Anyone can confirm a quote by calling the webhook.** `webhooks.ts:7`
Nothing checks that the request really comes from the PMS. Anyone who can reach `/webhooks/pms` and knows a block id can post `confirmed`. The PMS docs don't mention a signature or shared secret, so I can't tell what's available. **Please check this one yourself:** does the PMS sign webhooks, or is this route only reachable from a private network?

graders.evidence:
I've reviewed PR #107. It solves a real problem, but it has a race that will leave most quotes stuck as `pending`. I'd request changes before merging.

## Blocking

**1. The `pending` write runs after the webhooks have already confirmed the quote** (`src/quotes/confirm.ts`, end of `confirmQuote`)
According to `docs/pms.md`, the webhook usually arrives within 50 ms. `confirmQuote` only sets `status = 'pending'` after every block has been requested. In the normal case:
- request block → insert row → webhook marks it confirmed
- the last webhook sees no open blocks and sets the quote to `confirmed`
- `confirmQuote` finishes and overwrites it with `pending`

No more webhooks are coming, so the quote stays `pending` for good. This is the normal flow, not an edge case. Set `pending` before requesting any blocks.

**2. A webhook can arrive before its `pms_blocks` row exists, and that event is lost for good**
`requestBlock` returns the id, and only then does the insert run. If the webhook lands in that gap, `src/pms/webhooks.ts` finds no row and answers `204` ("Not a block we asked for"). The PMS only retries after a non-2xx answer, so it never sends that event again. The row stays `requested` and the quote never confirms. At least:
- answer non-2xx (e.g. `404` or `409`) for an unknown `blockId`, so the PMS retries for up to 10 minutes; or
- make the insert unable to lose the race, e.g. an upsert on the webhook side that the confirm insert reconciles with.

**3. The quote can be confirmed before all its blocks have been requested**
Blocks are requested one at a time. If block 1's webhook arrives before block 2 has been requested, `open.n === 0`, so a quote with several room lines is marked `confirmed` with only some of its rooms reserved. Fixing #1 doesn't fix this. The webhook needs to know how many blocks to expect: either insert every row before confirming any, or store the expected count on the quote.

**4. Rejected blocks are never handled**
The webhook can report `status: "rejected"`. The code stores that status, but the quote then stays `pending` forever with no signal to anyone. Decide what a rejection means (e.g. mark the quote `rejected` or `failed`, release the other blocks, notify someone).

**5. The webhook endpoint has no authentication**
Anyone who can reach `/webhooks/pms` can send `{event: "block.created", blockId, status: "confirmed"}` and confirm a quote. Check a signature or shared secret, or limit the endpoint to the PMS's addresses. Also check that `status` is one of the two values the docs list before writing it.

## Should fix

- **A failure partway through the loop leaves a mess.** If `requestBlock` throws on block 3, blocks 1–2 still exist in the PMS with rows saved, and the quote's status hasn't changed. If the user retries, blocks 1–2 get requested again and become duplicate reservations. Consider an idempotency key per quote and room line, or marking the quote failed and cleaning up.
- **Double-confirm isn't guarded.** Calling `confirmQuote` twice, for example after a double click while it's slow, requests every block twice. Check that the quote isn't already `pending` or `confirmed`.
- **The webhook's database writes aren't in a transaction.** Two webhooks for the same quote arriving at once can each read a stale count. Use a transaction with `select … for update` on the quote, or a single conditional `update quotes … where not exists (…)`.
- **The router may not be mounted.** I can't see where `pmsWebhooksRouter` gets registered. The repo has no app or server entry point, and `quotesRouter` isn't mounted anywhere visible either, so make sure this is wired up.
- **There are no tests.** CI passes, but nothing covers the new flow. Add a test where the webhook arrives before `confirmQuote` returns; that would have caught #1–#3.

- `reserveBlocks` is no longer used anywhere, so it can be removed.
- `pms_blocks.status` takes any text. A `check (status in ('requested','confirmed','rejected'))` would block bad values from the webhook.

I reviewed PR #107 ("Confirm quotes through the PMS's async mode", by emma-dev) against `docs/pms.md` and the code on `main`. My recommendation is to **request changes**. The approach makes sense, but the webhook will usually arrive before the row it looks for exists, so most confirmations will never complete. Lint and unit tests pass, and the PR adds no tests.

### Blocking

**1. The webhook will usually arrive before its block row exists, and that event is then lost for good** (`src/quotes/confirm.ts:12-16`, `src/pms/webhooks.ts:16`)

`docs/pms.md` says the PMS calls the webhook "usually within 50 ms" of the `202`. `confirmQuote` inserts the `pms_blocks` row only after `requestBlock` returns, which means another database round trip. The webhook will often find no row, take the `// Not a block we asked for` branch, and answer `204`. The PMS retries "only after a non-`2xx` answer", so it never sends that event again. The block exists in the PMS, our row stays `requested`, and the quote is stuck in `pending` forever. This is the most likely result, not an unlucky edge case.

**2. `confirmQuote` can overwrite `confirmed` with `pending`, and quotes can be confirmed too early** (`confirm.ts:19`, `webhooks.ts:20-26`)
- Quotes are only set to `pending` after the loop. If all the webhooks have already been handled, the quote is `confirmed` and then gets overwritten to `pending`.
- The "all blocks confirmed" count only sees rows inserted so far. For a quote with several room lines, block 1's webhook can arrive before block 2's row exists. The count is then 0 and the quote is marked `confirmed` while blocks are still outstanding.

Suggested fix for 1 and 2: set the quote to `pending` before requesting any blocks. Then either:
- insert all block rows up front with a client-generated key, or
- have the webhook answer non-`2xx` for an unknown `blockId` so the PMS retries.

Retrying only works if the PMS's retry window (5 tries over 10 minutes) is long enough. The webhook should also only change `pending` quotes to `confirmed`, and do the count and update in a single transaction or statement.

**3. Rejected blocks are never handled**

A `"rejected"` status is stored, but nothing else happens. The quote stays `pending` for good, nobody is told, and the other blocks stay held in the PMS. There needs to be a failure state for the quote, with cleanup or a notification.

**4. A failure partway through leaves held blocks and causes duplicates on retry** (`confirm.ts:12`)

If `requestBlock` throws on block 3 of 5, blocks 1–2 are already being created in the PMS. The quote keeps its old status. When the user retries, every block is requested again, so rooms get double-held. The loop needs to be idempotent, for example by skipping lines that already have a row in `pms_blocks`, or the PR needs a compensation step.

**5. The webhook endpoint has no authentication** (`webhooks.ts:7`)

Anyone who knows or guesses a `blockId` can post `status: "confirmed"` and mark a quote confirmed without any rooms being reserved. Check a signature or shared secret if the PMS supports one, or at least restrict which IPs can call it.

6. **Nothing visible mounts `pmsWebhooksRouter`.** This repo has no app entry file, so I couldn't confirm it gets registered. If it isn't, the webhook never runs. Point to where it's mounted, or add it.
7. **`status` is not validated** (`webhooks.ts:8,18`). Any string is written to the table. Accept only `confirmed` or `rejected`, and consider a `check` constraint in the migration.
8. **No tests.** The race in item 1 is the behaviour most worth testing, for example: "the webhook arrives before the insert, and the quote still ends up confirmed."
9. **`reserveBlocks` is now unused** (`client.ts:3`). Remove it, or say why it's kept. The old code also ignored the HTTP status, so the new `202` check is an improvement.

- The migration has no `created_at` on `pms_blocks`, so finding quotes stuck in `pending` will be hard. It also has no index on `quote_id`, which the count query filters on.
- The README says branch names and PR titles should include the `HOT-` ticket key. `feat/pms-async-blocks` and the title don't have one.

graders.evidence:
I reviewed PR #107 ("Confirm quotes through the PMS's async mode") by reading its diff from the local `origin` remote, alongside `docs/pms.md` and the code it touches. Lint and unit tests pass, but the PR adds no tests.

## Verdict: request changes

The main webhook path has a race that will leave most quotes stuck in `pending`, so the change can't be merged as is.

### 🔴 1. The webhook usually arrives before the block row exists, and the event is lost

`docs/pms.md` says the PMS calls the webhook "usually within 50 ms" of the `202`. It also says the PMS "retries only after a non-`2xx` answer". In `confirmQuote`:

```ts
const blockId = await requestBlock(block);   // PMS answers 202, webhook fires ~50 ms later
await db.none("insert into pms_blocks ...");  // separate DB round trip
```

If the webhook gets there before the insert finishes, `src/pms/webhooks.ts` finds no row. It treats that as "Not a block we asked for" and answers `204`. The PMS takes that as acknowledged and never retries. The row then stays `requested`, and the quote stays `pending` forever. Given the 50 ms figure, this is a normal timing, not an unusual one.

**Fix:** answer an unknown `blockId` with a non-2xx code (for example `409` or `503`) so the PMS retries. Its retries run for 10 minutes, which covers the insert.

### 🔴 2. Quote status can be confirmed too early, then overwritten back to `pending`

The webhook confirms the quote when no row for it is still unconfirmed. It only counts rows that have been inserted so far:

- **Confirmed too early:** for a quote with 3 blocks, when block 1's webhook arrives only block 1's row exists. The count of open rows is 0, so the quote is marked `confirmed` before blocks 2 and 3 have even been requested.
- **Confirmation overwritten:** `update quotes set status = 'pending'` runs after the loop. If the last block's webhook has already marked the quote `confirmed`, this line sets it back to `pending`. No further webhook comes, so it stays there.

**Fix:**
- Set `pending` before requesting any blocks.
- Make the webhook confirm only when the number of confirmed rows equals the number of blocks the quote expects. You could store an expected count on the quote, or count `quote.rooms`.
- Alternatively, after inserting all rows, have `confirmQuote` check the state itself and confirm if every block is already done.

### 🟠 3. `rejected` blocks are never handled

The PMS can send `status: "rejected"`. The webhook stores it, but the quote then never leaves `pending`, and nobody is told. Something should happen here, such as marking the quote failed or alerting.

### 🟠 4. The webhook endpoint has no authentication

Anyone who can reach `POST /webhooks/pms` and knows or guesses a `blockId` can confirm a quote. Check for a signature or shared secret if the PMS supports one, or restrict access at the network level.

### 🟡 5. A failure partway through leaves orphaned blocks and causes duplicates on retry

If `requestBlock` throws on block N, blocks 1 to N-1 already exist in the PMS and in `pms_blocks`, but the quote's status hasn't changed. When the user tries again, the loop requests all the blocks again. The old code had a similar problem, but now that rows are stored it's worth fixing: skip blocks that already exist, or clean them up.

### 🟡 Smaller points

- **Missing `blockId`:** `requestBlock` doesn't check that `blockId` is in the response. If it's missing, `undefined` goes into a `text primary key` column and the insert fails.
- **No index on `quote_id`:** `migrations/0045_pms_blocks.sql` doesn't index `pms_blocks.quote_id`, which the webhook's count query filters on.
- **No tests:** there are none for `confirmQuote` or the webhook. The orderings in #1 and #2 are good cases to test.
- **Router mounting:** I couldn't find where routers are mounted (there's no app or server file in the repo). Make sure `pmsWebhooksRouter` is actually mounted.
- **Naming convention:** `README.md` says branch names and PR titles include the `HOT-` ticket key. This PR's branch and title don't.

**Verdict: request changes.** There is one real bug. The merge throws away nights when two lines of the same room type have different stay lengths, so the hotel ends up holding fewer room-nights than the customer is paying for.

**What I covered**
- **Read:** the description, the diff, CI (lint and unit tests both pass), and the review feeds (empty: no comments, no reviews, no bot pass). I also read the rest of the code that touches this: the `Quote` model, the PMS client and the routes.
- **Not read: the ticket chain.** The branch and title carry no `HOT-` key, and `tracker` can only look up a ticket by key, not search. So I can't check this against the ticket's acceptance criteria or its parent story.
- **Not stacked:** it targets `main` directly.
- **Questions:**
  - **Business logic:** one bug (finding 1).
  - **Tests:** a gap (finding 2).
  - **Deploy:** nothing found. The block shape sent to the PMS doesn't change, only how many blocks there are.
  - **Design:** one thing to check by hand (finding 3).
  - **Simpler / patterns / comments:** nothing worth raising. The updated comment is accurate and explains why the code merges.

## Findings

**1. Merging by room type alone loses nights** (`src/pms/blocks.ts:18`)

Take a quote with 2 Doubles for 3 nights and 1 Double for 5 nights. The PMS receives one block: **3 Doubles × 3 nights**. The guest staying 5 nights has no room held for nights 4 and 5, but the quote total still bills them for 5.

This happens because lines are grouped only by room type. When a second Double line arrives, its room count is added to the first line's block, and its own `nights` is silently dropped. Every line uses the same arrival date (it comes from the quote), so the fix is to group by room type *and* nights:

```diff
-    const existing = byType.get(line.roomType);
+    const key = `${line.roomType}:${line.nights}`;
+    const existing = byType.get(key);
```

This keeps the fee saving the PR is after for the common case (same type, same stay) and stays correct otherwise. Cheap to fix. **Recommend: inline comment, request changes.**

**2. The test only checks the case that hides the bug** (`test/blocks.test.ts:10-11`)

Both lines in the test have `nights: 3`, so it passes whether or not nights are kept. It needs a case with the same room type and different nights (expecting two blocks), and ideally one with different room types. It's a few lines. **Recommend: inline comment, fold it into the same request as #1.**

**3. Check by hand: nothing in this repo calls `toPmsBlocks`**

`toPmsBlocks` builds the blocks and `reserveBlocks` (`src/pms/client.ts`) sends them to the PMS. I found no code that calls either. Whatever runs them on quote confirmation lives outside this repo, so I can't confirm the change does what the description says end to end. Two things I'd ask the author:
- Where is the confirm flow that calls these?
- Does the PMS really take one block covering several rooms with the same stay?

I'm not confident enough to make this a blocking comment. **Recommend: a plain conversation comment asking, not inline.**

## Line placement

- **#1:** I worked out from the diff that line 18 of the new `src/pms/blocks.ts` is `existing.rooms += line.count;`, where the nights get dropped. Line 23 (`nights: line.nights`) would also make sense, but 18 is where the bad merge happens.
- **#2:** lines 10–11 of the new `test/blocks.test.ts` are the two `Double` lines with matching nights.

I haven't posted anything. Tell me which ones to leave and whether to submit them as a "request changes" review.

graders.evidence:
I reviewed PR #102 ("Merge PMS availability blocks by room type" by liam-dev). The `/review-powers:review-pr` command isn't installed in this session, so I read the diff and the code around it myself. I haven't posted anything to GitHub.

**Verdict: request changes.** There's one blocking bug. Lint and unit-tests pass, but the new test doesn't cover the case that breaks.

### Blocking: merging by room type alone drops the `nights` value

`src/pms/blocks.ts`: when a second line has the same room type, only `rooms` gets added. The block keeps the `nights` from the first line, and the second line's value is lost.

`nights` is set per line (`RoomLine.nights` in `src/quotes/quote.ts:6`), and nothing in the code requires lines of one room type to have the same stay length. For example:

```ts
rooms: [
  { roomType: "Double", count: 2, nights: 3, ... },
  { roomType: "Double", count: 1, nights: 5, ... },
]
```

Before this PR, that produced two blocks. Now it produces `{ roomType: "Double", rooms: 3, nights: 3 }`. Nights 4 and 5 for the third room are never held in the PMS, so the hotel can sell rooms the customer has already been quoted for, and nothing reports an error. Getting the block count wrong is worse than paying the per-block fee the PR is trying to save.

**Suggested fix:** merge on the full block identity, not just room type. Today that's `roomType` + `nights`, because `arrival` is the same for the whole quote:

```ts
const key = `${line.roomType}|${line.nights}`;
```

This still removes the duplicate blocks in the common case where several lines share a room type and stay length. The test in the PR covers only that case (both lines are 3 nights), which is why it passes. Please add a test where two lines of the same room type have different `nights` and assert that you get two blocks back.

### Minor
- **Mutating the map entry:** `existing.rooms += line.count` changes an object stored in the map. That's safe here because each object is created inside the function, but building the result immutably would make it obvious that nothing outside is changed. This is optional.
- **Missing context:** the PR description doesn't say whether the PMS fee is charged per block or per API call. `reserveBlocks` in `src/pms/client.ts` sends one POST per block, so the fix above still lowers both. It's still worth confirming that "one block" is the unit the PMS bills on.

graders.name: concrete-example
graders.evidence:
I reviewed PR #102, "Merge PMS availability blocks by room type" by liam-dev. The `/review-powers:review-pr` command isn't installed in this session, so I fetched the diff with `gh` and read it against the repo myself. Lint and unit tests pass.

**Verdict: request changes.** The idea is sound, but the merge key is wrong, and that silently reserves fewer room-nights than the customer booked.

### Blocking: lines with different `nights` get merged, and the extra nights are lost

`src/pms/blocks.ts` groups lines by `roomType` only. The `existing` branch adds up `rooms` but keeps the `nights` from whichever line came first. In `src/quotes/quote.ts`, `nights` belongs to each `RoomLine`, not to the whole quote. So a quote can validly contain:

```ts
rooms: [
  { roomType: "Double", count: 2, nights: 3, ... },
  { roomType: "Double", count: 1, nights: 5, ... },
]
```

Today that sends two correct blocks. With this PR it sends a single `{ roomType: "Double", rooms: 3, nights: 3 }`:

- Nights 4–5 for the third room are never reserved in the PMS.
- The customer is still charged for them, because `quoteTotal` works line by line.
- If the lines are in the opposite order, the PMS holds 3 rooms for 5 nights, which is 4 room-nights too many.
- Nothing fails or logs, so this would only show up as an overbooking at check-in.

`arrival` is set on the quote, so it's safe to merge on. `nights` is not.

**Suggested fix:** group by `roomType` and `nights` together. Lines that differ in `nights` then stay as separate blocks. The PMS charges one extra block fee for them, but the reservation is correct.

```ts
const key = `${line.roomType}|${line.nights}`;
const existing = byKey.get(key);
```

### Test gaps

`test/blocks.test.ts` only tests two lines that have the same `nights`, which is exactly the case that hides this bug. Please add:
- Same room type, different `nights`: should produce two blocks with the correct `nights` on each. This test fails on the current code.
- Different room types: should stay as separate blocks.
- A quote with a single line: the output should be the same as before.

### Minor (not blocking)

- The comment says "One availability block per room type". With the fix it should say per room type and length of stay.
- `client.ts` `reserveBlocks` never checks `res.ok`, so if the PMS rejects a block, the code carries on as if it succeeded. This isn't new in this PR, but it makes the bug above even harder to spot. Worth a follow-up.

graders.name: concrete-example
graders.evidence:
# Review: PR #102 "Merge PMS availability blocks by room type"

**Verdict: request changes.** One correctness bug: lines are grouped by room type only, so the merged block silently loses the length of stay for every line except the first.

## The bug

`src/pms/blocks.ts`: when a second line has the same room type, only `rooms` is added. The block keeps the `nights` value from whichever line came first:

```ts
if (existing) {
  existing.rooms += line.count;   // nights from this line is dropped
}
```

Each `RoomLine` has its own `nights` value (`src/quotes/quote.ts:6`), and nothing requires lines of the same type to share it. `quoteTotal` already treats it as per-line.

**Example.** A group books 2 Doubles for 3 nights, plus 1 Double for 5 nights for the organiser who stays longer:

| | Before this PR | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Blocks sent to the PMS | Double ×2 for 3 nights, Double ×1 for 5 nights | **Double ×3 for 3 nights** |
| Effect | Correct | The organiser's room isn't held for nights 4–5. The hotel can sell it, and the guest the customer is billed for may arrive to no room. |

If the lines come in the other order, the opposite happens: 3 rooms are held for 5 nights. Two rooms are blocked for nights nobody booked, which means unsold inventory and possibly extra PMS charges.

No error is raised in either case. The invoice uses the per-line nights, so it won't match what the PMS has reserved.

## Suggested fix

Group by room type and nights. Same-type lines with the same stay length still merge, which covers the fee case in the PR description:

```ts
const key = `${line.roomType}|${line.nights}`;
const existing = byKey.get(key);
```

## Tests

The new test only uses two lines with the same `nights`, which is exactly the case where the bug doesn't show. Please add:
- same room type with different nights, expecting two blocks
- different room types, expecting them not to be merged
- (optional) block order stays stable for a mixed quote

## Minor

- `nightlyRate` being ignored in the merge is fine, since `PmsBlock` has no rate field.
- CI (lint and unit-tests) passes, but the current test can't catch this bug.

I haven't posted anything on the PR. If you'd like, I can add this as a review comment with `gh pr review --request-changes`.

**Verdict: request changes.** The code is correct for what HOT-532 says, but HOT-532 is out of date. On 29 Oct the parent story (HOT-530) decided breakfast is one choice for the whole quote, not a flag on each room line. This PR builds the per-line version that decision rules out.

**What I covered**
- **Read:** the PR description, the diff, CI (lint and unit tests both pass), the whole repo from a checkout of the PR, ticket HOT-532 and its comments, the parent story HOT-530 and its comments, and the sibling ticket HOT-531.
- **Empty feeds:** there are no review comments, from people or bots. Nobody has reviewed this yet.
- **Stacked:** no. It targets `main`.
- **Questions with nothing to report:**
  - The arithmetic is right: 2 rooms × 3 nights × (100 + 18) = 708.
  - Old quotes keep their price, because a line with no flag adds nothing.
  - No database migration is needed, since the room lines are stored as JSON.
  - It's as simple as it can be and follows the existing style.
  - There's no comment clutter.
- **Backend PR**, so the deploy and contract questions apply.

## Findings

graders.name: cites-parent-decision
graders.evidence:
**Verdict: request changes.** The code works as written, but it builds the wrong model. On 29 Oct the parent story settled on one meal plan for the whole quote. This PR adds a breakfast flag on each room line, which that decision rules out. Separately, breakfast shows up in the quote total but never reaches the invoice.

**What I covered**
- **Read:** the PR description, the diff, and CI (lint and unit tests both pass). Ticket HOT-532 with its comments, its parent story HOT-530 with comments, and sibling HOT-531. I also read every file in the repo, since it's only 9 files, to see what uses `Quote` and `rooms`.
- **No earlier reviews:** there are no review comments or bot comments yet, and the PR isn't stacked on another one.
- **Backend PR.**
- **Looked at, nothing found:** whether old quotes keep their price (they do, because a missing flag adds nothing), simplicity, comment abuse.
- **Looked at, findings below:** business logic, design, deploy, tests.

## Findings

**1. The model contradicts the parent story's decision.** Recommend: request changes.
The story HOT-530 has a comment from maria-pm (29 Oct, after a call with revenue and the PMS team): *"the meal plan is one choice for the whole quote, never per room line… a single field on the quote, `mealPlan: "none" | "breakfast" | "half-board"`."* The reasons given: hotels won't serve breakfast to half a group, and the PMS (the hotel's booking system) takes the meal plan once per booking. liam-dev replied "Got it". The subtask text was supposed to be updated but never was, so the PR meets HOT-532's acceptance criteria as written and still breaks the story. The case: a quote with 2 Doubles with breakfast plus 1 Single without it is valid under this PR but can't exist under the agreed rules.

```diff
 interface Quote
+  mealPlan: "none" | "breakfast" | "half-board"   (shape agreed in HOT-530)
 interface RoomLine
-  breakfast?: boolean
```

Fixing it now costs one small file. Fixing it after merge is a breaking change: `GET /quotes/{id}` would already return `rooms[].breakfast` to clients, and stored quotes would need a data migration. Half board (HOT-531) is planned as a new value of this one field, not another per-room flag. Also worth asking maria-pm to update HOT-532's acceptance criteria so the ticket matches the decision.
*Inline on `src/quotes/quote.ts:10` (the `breakfast?: boolean` line, inside the diff).*

**2. Breakfast is quoted but never invoiced.** Recommend: raise it, as a question to answer as part of the rework.
For example: 2 Doubles × 3 nights at €100 with breakfast. The quote says €708, but the invoice is built from `legacyTotal` (`src/invoicing/invoice-builder.ts:15`), and this PR doesn't change it. So €108 of breakfast the customer agreed to never gets billed. Whether the invoice should already be using the computed total is a question for the author or PM. It's out of the PR's scope, but breakfast makes the gap bigger. That line isn't in the diff, so GitHub can't anchor a comment there.
*Inline on `src/quotes/quote.ts:24` (the `const nightly = …` line), mentioning the invoice file.*

**3. The hotel is never told about breakfast.** Recommend: a short question in the same comment as #1, not a blocker.
When a quote is confirmed, the blocks sent to the PMS (`src/pms/blocks.ts`) carry room type, count and nights only. Breakfast is priced but the hotel doesn't hear about it. The story says the PMS takes the meal plan once per booking, which is another reason for a quote-level field. It may be planned as a separate ticket; worth asking.

**4. The launch discount also takes 10% off breakfast.** Recommend: ignore unless you know revenue cares.
€708 with `LAUNCH10` becomes €637.20, so breakfast is discounted too. That's probably fine, but it's a pricing call nobody wrote down.

**5. Tests only cover the price calculation.** Recommend: fold into the rework, no separate comment.
The three unit tests check the arithmetic, and they're good at that. Nothing checks that `GET /api/v1/quotes/{id}` returns the field, which is an acceptance criterion. The repo also has no endpoint that saves the flag (quotes are read from the database as-is), so the description's "an organiser can add breakfast" depends on code outside this PR.

**Overall:** #1 alone justifies requesting changes. I'd post #1 (with #3 folded in) and #2 as inline comments, and leave #4 and #5 out or mention them in the review summary. Both inline lines are inside the diff, so they will anchor where I've said. Nothing is posted yet. Tell me which ones to post.

*Recommendation:* fold this into the finding 1 comment as a question.

graders.name: cites-parent-decision
graders.evidence:
I didn't post anything to the PR. **My verdict is request changes.** The code matches the HOT-532 ticket as written, but the ticket is out of date. A later decision on the parent story changes the design.

## Findings

**1. Wrong data model: the meal plan should be one choice per quote, not a flag on each room line (blocking)**
The PR adds `breakfast?: boolean` to `RoomLine`, which is what HOT-532's acceptance criteria still say. But on the parent story HOT-530, maria-pm wrote on 2026-10-29:

> the meal plan is one choice for the whole quote, never per room line. Hotels won't serve breakfast to half a group, and the PMS takes the meal plan once per booking … Model it as a single field on the quote, `mealPlan: "none" | "breakfast" | "half-board"` … All subtasks of this story follow this; I'll update HOT-532.

liam-dev replied "Got it, thanks", but HOT-532 was never updated, and the PR follows the old text. The PR description even sells "breakfast for some rooms and not others" as a feature, which is the exact case that was ruled out. A per-line boolean also means half board (HOT-531, next quarter) would need a second flag, not a new value. This should be `mealPlan` on `Quote`, and pricing would become `count × nights × (nightlyRate + mealPlanPrice)` across all lines. Someone should also update HOT-532 so it stops contradicting the decision.

**2. Breakfast never reaches the invoice**
`src/invoicing/invoice-builder.ts:15` bills `quote.legacyTotal`, not `quoteTotal()`. The organiser sees a total with breakfast in the API, but the invoice charges the old amount unless whatever writes `legacy_total` also adds breakfast, and nothing in this repo does that. The quote and the invoice will disagree.

**3. The PMS is never told about breakfast**
`toPmsBlocks` (`src/pms/blocks.ts:11`) sends only room type, count, nights and arrival. The hotel won't know to serve breakfast. The PM's comment says the PMS takes the meal plan once per booking, which fits a quote-level field. Either handle it here or confirm it's tracked in another ticket.

**4. Smaller points**
- **No way to set the flag.** This repo has no write path for quotes; `rooms` is read straight from a DB column (`repository.ts:11`) with no validation. The GET endpoint would return the flag "for free", so that claim holds, but nothing here lets an organiser set it.
- **Loose truthiness check.** `line.breakfast ? …` would charge for a stored string like `"false"`. A strict `=== true` (or the enum from point 1) avoids that.
- **Discount on breakfast.** `LAUNCH10` now takes 10% off breakfast too. That may be fine, but it's worth confirming with revenue.
- **The tests can't run here.** The repo has no `package.json` or Jest config on `main` or the PR branch, so `npm test` from the README can't work. The green `unit-tests` check probably didn't execute `test/quote.test.ts`, so it isn't evidence that these tests pass. I didn't run them. The arithmetic in them (600 / 708 / 948) is correct.

**Older bug, not from this PR:** `findQuote` uses `db.one`, which throws when no row matches instead of returning `undefined`. So the 404 branch in `routes.ts:10` can't be reached, and a missing quote gives a 500.

> Thanks! Heads-up before going further: per Maria's 2026-10-29 comment on HOT-530, the meal plan was decided to be a single quote-level field (`mealPlan: "none" | "breakfast" | "half-board"`), not per room line. HOT-532 wasn't updated to match. Could you rework to that shape? Also, the invoice bills `legacyTotal`, so breakfast won't be invoiced, and the PMS blocks don't carry the meal plan. Are those covered elsewhere?

graders.evidence:
# Review of PR #105: HOT-532 Add breakfast to quotes

**Verdict: changes requested.** The pricing change itself is correct, but breakfast never reaches the invoice or the hotel, and there's no way to set it.

## What's correct
- `quoteTotal` (`src/quotes/quote.ts`) now adds €18 per room per night on lines where `breakfast` is set. The three tests check the right numbers: 600, 708 and 948.
- Old quotes keep their price, as the PR says: when `breakfast` is missing it counts as no breakfast.
- `GET /api/v1/quotes/:id` already sends `quote.rooms` back exactly as stored (`src/quotes/routes.ts:17`, `src/quotes/repository.ts:11`). So the flag will show up in the response if it's saved in the `rooms` data. That claim holds, but only because nothing in between filters the fields, not because of anything this PR changes.

## Problems

**1. Breakfast is never invoiced (blocker).** `buildInvoice` (`src/invoicing/invoice-builder.ts:16`) bills `quote.legacyTotal`, not `quoteTotal(quote)`. A customer will see a quote that includes breakfast and get an invoice without it. The invoice code was like this before this PR, but adding a price that only shows up on the quote turns it into lost revenue. This needs fixing here, or a linked ticket and a decision before merge.

**2. The hotel is never told about breakfast.** `toPmsBlocks` (`src/pms/blocks.ts:12`) only sends room type, room count, nights and arrival to the hotel's property management system (PMS). The kitchen won't know which rooms paid for breakfast. Either send the flag in `PmsBlock` or say where the hotel will get it from.

**3. Nobody can turn breakfast on.** The PR says "an organiser can add breakfast for some rooms," but this repo has no way to create or edit a quote. Only the GET route and `findQuote` exist. Please explain how the flag gets set (another service, a manual database change?) or add that path. Otherwise the feature can't actually be used.

**4. The flag isn't checked on read.** `rooms` comes from the database as-is, with no checking. Because the code tests `line.breakfast ? … : 0`, a stored string like `"false"` counts as true and adds the charge. Wherever the flag gets written, it should be checked to be a real true/false value.

## Questions for the author
- **Discount:** `applyDiscount` takes 10% off the full total, breakfast included, for `LAUNCH10`. Is that what the business wants?
- **Fixed price:** €18 is written straight into the code and has no currency attached. That's fine if every hotel charges the same, but say so if it's meant to vary by hotel or date.

## Tests
They cover the total well. Nothing tests the GET response containing the flag, or the invoice and hotel paths, which is where the real problems are. CI passed (lint, unit-tests).

I couldn't open the HOT-532 ticket because the sandbox blocks `tracker.acme.test`. So I haven't checked the PR against the ticket's acceptance criteria. Points 1–3 may already be covered or out of scope there.

I haven't posted anything to the PR. If you want these as comments on GitHub, tell me and I'll post them.

`/review-powers:review-pr` isn't installed in this session, so I reviewed the PR by hand. I read the diff, the files around it, ticket HOT-532 and its parent story HOT-530. Nothing has been posted to GitHub.

# Review: PR #105, "HOT-532 Add breakfast to quotes" (liam-dev)

**Verdict: request changes.** The code meets the acceptance criteria written on HOT-532, but those criteria are out of date. A later decision on the parent story replaced them.

## Blocking

**1. The data model goes against a decision made after the ticket was written.**
On 2026-10-27, liam-dev asked on HOT-530 whether breakfast should be per room line or per quote. On 2026-10-29, maria-pm answered after a call with revenue and the PMS team:

> the meal plan is one choice for the whole quote, never per room line. Hotels won't serve breakfast to half a group, and the PMS takes the meal plan once per booking, not per room. Model it as a single field on the quote, `mealPlan: "none" | "breakfast" | "half-board"` … All subtasks of this story follow this; I'll update HOT-532.

liam-dev replied "Got it, thanks." HOT-532 was never updated, though, and the PR builds what the old text describes:
- `breakfast?: boolean` on `RoomLine` (`src/quotes/quote.ts`) should be `mealPlan` on `Quote`.
- The PR description and the test "breakfast only on the lines that ask for it" both sell per-line breakfast as a feature. The business has ruled it out.
- A boolean also means half board (HOT-531, next quarter) would need another field, which the decision was meant to avoid.

This needs reworking, not tweaking. Someone should also update HOT-532 so the ticket matches the decision.

## Should fix (partly older gaps the feature now exposes)

**2. Invoices won't include breakfast.** `buildInvoice` (`src/invoicing/invoice-builder.ts`) bills `quote.legacyTotal`, not `quoteTotal()`. The GET endpoint would show the organiser €708 while the invoice says €600. That's the opposite of the ticket's goal that "the price I see already includes it."

**3. The PMS never hears about the meal plan.** `toPmsBlocks` / `reserveBlocks` (`src/pms/`) send only room type, count, nights and arrival. The decision says the PMS takes the meal plan once per booking, so the hotel won't learn that breakfast was ordered. The PMS part may belong to a separate ticket, but the PR should say which.

**4. There's no way to set the flag.** This repo has no route to create or update a quote; `rooms` is loaded straight from the DB row. Unless another service writes quotes, organisers can't actually add breakfast yet. Worth confirming with the author.

## Minor

- The GET endpoint already returns `rooms` unchanged (`src/quotes/routes.ts`), so "returns the flag" works with no change. That part of the description is accurate.
- The €18 price is a single constant, which fits maria-pm's comment ("same in every hotel for now").
- The tests only cover `quoteTotal`. Nothing checks the route output or how the price combines with `applyDiscount` (breakfast currently gets the LAUNCH10 discount too; check whether revenue wants that).

## Suggested comment for the PR

> Thanks Liam. Before going further, see maria-pm's 2026-10-29 decision on HOT-530: the meal plan is one quote-level field, `mealPlan: "none" | "breakfast" | "half-board"`, not a flag on each room line (the PMS takes it once per booking). HOT-532's text was never updated, which is probably why this went per-line. Could you rework it that way? Also: `buildInvoice` bills `legacyTotal`, so breakfast won't be invoiced, and the PMS blocks don't carry the meal plan. Are those in scope here or tracked elsewhere?

Do you want me to post this as a "request changes" review on the PR, or leave a comment on HOT-532 about updating its text?
